title: fscale verify --json output
description: The report printed by `fscale verify --json`. Steps are listed in the order they run: check, then lint, typecheck and test at the repo root, then the same three for each project found below the root.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this format. Changes only on a breaking change.

version.description: The firescale version that produced the report.

ok.description: True when the exit code is 0: result is ok or partial.

result.description: ok: every step ran and passed. partial: nothing failed, but at least one step was skipped because no command was found. failed: a step failed, or steps were skipped while verify.failOnSkipped is on. setup-needed: nothing failed in the code, but at least one step could not run because the environment is not set up. stopped: verify was stopped by Ctrl+C or a termination signal before every step finished; the steps that finished are reported.

runner.description: How the commands of the repo root were chosen: all three from the config, Nx, Turborepo, package.json scripts, Cargo, a Python or Go project at the root, none found, or projects when the root has no commands of its own and the projects below it supply them.

stepsTotal.description: Steps that should run: every step except the ones whose status is off or not-affected.

stepsRun.description: Steps with a result: passed (now or from the cache), failed or needs setup.

failOnSkipped.description: The verify.failOnSkipped setting of the config.

failedStep.description: Name of the first step that failed or needs setup. Every one is in steps and in the headline. Absent when no step failed.

failedProject.description: Folder of the project of failedStep. Absent when that step belongs to the repo root.

rerun.description: The command of failedStep, to run again after fixing it, from the folder in failedProject when that is present. Absent when no step failed.

warnings.description: One sentence that names the skipped steps and says how to give them a command. Absent when nothing was skipped.

project.description: Folder of the project the step belongs to, where its command runs. "." for a project at the repo root that the root's own commands do not cover. Absent for a step of the repo root.

kind.description: The kind of that project. Absent for a root step and for a folder that is only named in the config.

status.description: failed: the command failed. setup-needed: the command could not do its work because the environment is not ready (a dependency is not installed, or a program is not on the PATH); not a problem in the code. timed-out: the command gave no result within its time limit, so it was stopped with every process it started. stopped: verify was stopped while the command ran, so it was stopped with every process it started. skipped: no command was found, so nothing was verified. not-run: an earlier step of the same project (or the check) failed, or verify was stopped, so this one was not started. off: not run on purpose, because the config turns it off or another step covers it. not-affected: --affected found that no change reaches the step's project, so it was not run (ADR 0032); not the same as skipped.

command.description: The command that ran, or would have. Absent for a skipped step and for one that is off.

exitCode.description: Exit code of the command. Absent when the step did not run or was killed by a signal.

detail.description: One line about the outcome: a count, the command, or why the step did not run.

outputTail.description: The last lines of the output of a step that failed, timed out or needs setup, without colour codes. Absent otherwise.

fix.description: For a step that needs setup, or that timed out with output that shows a setup problem: the command that sets the environment up (installs dependencies, or starts services with Docker Compose), run from the project's folder. Absent when no command is known.

timeoutMs.description: For a step that timed out: its time limit, in milliseconds.

timeoutKey.description: For a step that timed out: the config key that sets its time limit.

tests.description: For a step that ran pytest or unittest: the tests its output counted (ADR 0035).

firstError.description: For a pytest step that was stopped early or timed out: the text of its first error, from one more run of its command with --maxfail=1 (ADR 0035). Connection strings' user and password are shown as ***.

cache.description: Set when the step was not run now: it passed before on the same inputs, and that pass came from the step cache (ADR 0036). Its status is passed and its durationMs is 0.

durationMs.description: How long the step took when it ran.

skipped.description: Every step that was skipped because no command was found. Empty when result is ok.

project.description: Folder of the project. Absent for the repo root.

notes.description: Things worth knowing that are not failures: Python projects whose commands use python from the PATH because no virtual environment was found for them. Absent when there are none.

scope.description: all: every project. affected: --affected ran only the projects a change reaches, so result describes those, not the whole repo.

affected.description: Present when scope is affected: which projects ran and why (ADR 0032).

base.description: The --base ref, or null when only uncommitted and untracked changes count.

everything.description: True when every project is affected: a changed file no project owns, a root lockfile, a CI file, a Compose file or the firescale config, no commit to compare with, or nothing to compare (no --base and a clean tree).

reason.description: Why every project is affected. Absent when everything is false.

projectsTotal.description: Units with steps: each project, and the repo root's own steps as one.

project.description: Folder of the project. Absent for the repo root's own steps.

reason.description: Why it ran (a changed file, or the node it depends on), or why it did not.

cache.description: What the step cache did (ADR 0036). Absent when it was not used.

read.description: false with --no-cache: every step ran, and passes were still stored.

hits.description: Steps whose pass came from the cache instead of running now.

savedMs.description: What those steps took when they last ran, in milliseconds.
